steps.text: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat and stir in ground beef and onion. Cook and stir until beef is crumbly, evenly browned, and no longer pink, about 10 minutes. Drain and discard any excess grease. Stir in ketchup, water, brown sugar, Worcestershire sauce, mustard, vinegar, chili powder, garlic powder, onion powder, and salt.
Bring beef mixture to a boil over high heat. Reduce heat to low; cover and simmer until sauce has thickened, 30 to 40 minutes. Serve on buns.

raw_recipe.headline: Sloppy Joe Sandwiches
raw_recipe.description: This sloppy joe recipe is quick and inexpensive. In addition to putting it on rolls, try this slightly sweet beef mixture over rice, biscuits, or baked potatoes.
raw_recipe.name: Sloppy Joe Sandwiches

review.reviewBody: Soooo good. I used two parts ketchup to one part BBQ sauce and used Dijon mustard and added a sweet pepper. My hungry teenage son applauds. This is a definite keeper.

Very good! Will definitely make this again! I used apple cider vinegar and two cloves of garlic instead of garlic powder, and I used chicken instead of beef. I added a chopped tomato with the liquid, and mashed the cooked meat with a potato masher to get it nice and tiny. Simmered all the juice into the meat. Yum yum!

Just exactly the recipe I was looking for. This is a perfect swap for Manwich and so easy to make. Followed directions except I doubled it and added some chopped green & red pepper to the mix. I made this again using slow cooker, browned the meat and onions and put everything in the slow cooker on LOW for about 6 hours. Perfection once again!

Made this recipe mostly as written. The most important things I noticed was the lack of liquid. I added 3/4 cup of beef broth which allowed the seasonings and the onions to simmer to meld the flavors. Also only cook the burger till it's no longer pink. 1 tsp brown sugar is plenty. Ketchup adds plenty of sweetness on it's own. Optional, to taste, add a pinch of ground cayenne or 1/3 chopped fresh chili without the seeds.

Very good recipe I was impressed, although I did some slight changes because I do not like too sweet of sloppy joes. Also notice the proportions given in their recipe is for only .5 Lb of ground beef.
First change was a 50/50 ratio of ketchup and plain tomato sauce, second was adding a pinch more of chili powder, black pepper, vinegar, and Worcestershire sauce to make-up for the lack of ketchup. 
Another review stated not to be afraid of the vinegar it offsets the sweetness, very true!

This was delicious. These were a little sweet, a little tangy, a little tomatoey, and a lot of tasty flavor. I used mini rolls and made sliders, so they were more bite sized. I used dried minced onion. I did season the beef with Season-All as it was cooking and skipped the salt at the end. I did have to add more water as this was getting too thick while it did that long simmer. I kept adding more water as needed to keep the consistency from drying out. This is one of the better sloppy joe recipes on here. This is definitely kid friendly and picky eater approved. 4.5 stars

WOW! Was this outstanding as the recipe called for. I made a double batch for leftovers.

Nothing needs to be changed. This recipe is Outstanding just the way it is.

 I decided I would experiment by adding a can of mushrooms (just because we love mushrooms) and what I found to put this dish way over the top, added a teaspoon of Good quality liquid smoke.

The recipe sauce is so good in this dish, I want to try it out on a smoked pork butt For pulled pork sammies and smoked ribs.
this was very good, did add fresh garlic and a little finely chopped green pepper(3-4 Tbsp) and used cider vinegar instead of white liked my grandmother used too. I'll make this again

Very easy recipe. I had to substitute balsamic vinegar for white vinegar as that is what I had. I also added some chopped green pepper. Tastes much better than using prepared sloppy joe sauce. I also used lean ground turkey instead of ground beef. I served it on slices of French bread with cheesy broccoli.
I doubled the recipe and this was easy to make and all ingredients on hand. I thought it was a little sweet so next time I will use less brown sugar. Better flavor than the canned or packaged type.
My fiance hates onions and tomatoes. So, I took out the ketchup and brown sugar and used bbq sauce. Also left out the real onions. It turned out awesome!
Easy to make recipe. Great flavor and no hard to find ingredients. Also, no artificial ingredients! Only change made was the addition of a green pepper when cooking the ground beef and onions.
we loved it i used jalapeno mustard for regular mustard a keeper for sure !!

I was looking for a recipe with no celery as I have people allergic to it. Stumbled on this recipe and now has become a family favorite celery or not ! I have request for recipe all the time and you can tweek accordingly g to your taste with the amount of vinegar as it takes on a much different flavor!
Amazing!!!!!
Love this! My mother used to serve it over noodles an it was great!
I have made this twice. It's so much better than that canned sauce. So yummy! I didn't change anything.

As soon as I found this recipe years ago, it's the only sloppy joes we eat. Never from the can ever again! I follow recipe as written and then add 1/2 - 3/4 cup of salsa to the mixture. The salsa adds more dimension and spice. It is truly a family favorite!
Husband loved it. Made it exactly as written.
Very good ,, will make again
